50:1: Interpretation of Surah Qaf This surah is the first surah of Al-Hizb Al-Mufassal according to the correct view, and it was also said that it is from Al-Hujurat. As for what the common people say that it is from Amma, it has no basis and none of the respected scholars may God be pleased with them have said it as far as we know. The evidence that this surah is the first of the Mufassal is what Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunan in the chapter on dividing the Qur’an into parts. Then he said: Musaddad told us, Qaran bin Tamam told us, Abdullah bin Saeed Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Abu Khalid, Sulayman bin Hayyan told us - and this is his wording - on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Ya’la, on the authority of Uthman bin Abdullah bin Aws, on the authority of his grandfather. Abdullah bin Saeed said: Aws bin Hudhayfah told me, then they agreed. He said: We came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a delegation from Thaqeef. He said: The allies stayed with Al-Mugheerah bin Shu’bah, may God be pleased with him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, housed Banu Malik in a tent of his. Musaddad said: He was in the delegation from Thaqeef who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would come to us every night after the evening prayer and talk to us. Abu Saeed said: Standing on his feet until he would alternate between his feet from the length of standing. Most of what he, may God bless him and grant him peace, would tell us was what he encountered from his people, the Quraysh. Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say: We are not equal, and we were… Weak and humiliated - Musaddad said in Mecca - so when we went out to Medina, the war was raging between us and them, we were victorious over them and they were victorious over us. One night he was slow to come to us, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to us at a time he used to do so, so we said: You were slow to come to us tonight. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: My portion of the Qur’an came to me and I did not want to come until I finished it. Aws said: I asked the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) how they divided the Qur’an into portions. They said: Three, five, seven, nine, eleven, and thirteen. And the Hizb al-Mufassal alone, and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah on the authority of Abu Khalid al-Ahmar with it, and Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi on the authority of Abdullah bin Abd al-Rahman - he is Ibn Ya'la al-Taifi with it. If this is known, and you count forty-eight Surahs, then the one after them is Surah Qaf. Its explanation is three: Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, and An-Nisa. Five: Al-Ma'idah, Al-An'am, Al-A'raf, Al-Anfal, and Bara'ah. Seven: Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, Ar-Ra'd, Ibrahim, Al-Hijr, and An-Nahl. Nine: Subhan, Al-Kahf, Maryam, Ta-Ha, Al-Anbiya', Al-Hajj, Al-Mu'minoon, An-Nur, and Al-Furqan. Eleven: Ash-Shu'ara', An-Naml, Al-Qasas, Al-'Ankabut, Ar-Rum, Luqman, Alif-Lam-Sajdah, Al-Ahzab, Saba', Fatir, and Yasin. Thirteen: As-Saffat, Sad, Az-Zumar, Ghafir, Ha-Mim As-Sajdah, Ha-Mim 'Ain Sin Qaf, Az-Zukhruf, Ad-Dukhan, Al-Jathiyah, Al-Ahqaf, Al-Fath, and Al-Hujurat. Then after that is the Hizb al-Mufassal as the Companions may God be pleased with them said. It was determined that the beginning of it is Surat Qaf. And this is what we said, and praise and thanks be to God. Imam Ahmad said: Abdur-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, Malik told us, on the authority of Damrah bin Saeed, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah, that Umar bin Al-Khattab asked Abu Waqid Al-Laithi: What did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recite on Eid? He said: Qaf and it is approaching. Muslim and the four Sunan scholars narrated it from the hadith of Malik with it. In a narration by Muslim, on the authority of Falih, on the authority of Damrah, on the authority of Ubaidullah, on the authority of Abu Waqid, he said: Umar may God be pleased with him asked me, and he mentioned it. Another hadith Ahmad said: Ya`qub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Bakr bin Amr bin Hazm told me, on the authority of Yahya bin Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Sa`d bin Zararah, on the authority of Umm Hisham bint Haritha, who said: Our oven and the oven of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were the same for two years or a year and part of a year, and I did not learn Qaf, by the Glorious Qur’an except from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he used to recite it every Friday from the pulpit when he addressed the people. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq with it. Abu Dawud said: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Ma`n, on the authority of the daughter of Al-Harith bin An-Nu`man, who said: I did not memorize Qaf except from the mouth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he addressed the people with it every Friday. She said: Our oven and the oven of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were one. This is how Muslim, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah. The point is that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite this surah at major gatherings, such as Eid and Friday prayers, because it includes information about the beginning of creation, resurrection, the afterlife, the rising and the reckoning, Paradise and Hell, reward and punishment, encouragement and intimidation. And God knows best. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful "Qaf": A letter of the alphabet mentioned at the beginning of the surahs, such as the Almighty’s saying: Sad, “Nun,” Alif, Lam, Meem, “Ta, Seen,” and the like. This was said by Mujahid and others. We have already discussed it at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no need to repeat it. It has been narrated from some of the early generations that they said: Qaf is a mountain that surrounds the entire earth, and it is called Mount Qaf. It seems that this, and God knows best, is one of the fables of the Children of Israel that some people took from them when they saw the permissibility of narrating from them what is neither true nor false. I believe that this and its likes and similar things are the fabrications of some of their heretics, with which they confuse people about their religion, just as in this nation, despite the great status of its scholars, hadith masters, and imams, hadiths from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were fabricated, and the covenant is not very old. So how about the nation of the Children of Israel, with its long history, the small number of critical hadith masters among them, their drinking of alcohol, and their scholars distorting words from their places and changing the books and verses of God? The Lawgiver only permitted narration from them in His saying: “And narrate from The Children of Israel, and there is no harm in what the mind may permit. As for what the mind rejects and judges to be false and is most likely to be false, then it is not of this type, and God knows best. Many of the early commentators, as well as a large group of later commentators, have frequently narrated from the books of the People of the Book in their interpretation of the Glorious Qur’an, and there is no need for their reports, praise and thanks be to God, to the point that Imam Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim al-Razi, may God have mercy on him, mentioned here a strange narration whose chain of transmission is not authentic on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. He said: My father told us, saying: I told him on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Makhzumi, who told us on the authority of Layth ibn Abi Salim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: God Almighty created, beyond this earth, a sea surrounding it. Then He created, beyond that sea, a mountain called Qaf, with the lowest heaven raised above it. Then God Almighty created, beyond that mountain, an earth seven times the size of that earth. Then He created, beyond that, a sea surrounding it. Then He created, beyond that, a mountain called Qaf, with the second heaven raised above it, until He counted seven earths, seven seas, seven mountains, and seven heavens. He said, and that is in the words of God Almighty: “And the sea, after it, will be replenished by seven more.” "Abhar", so its chain of transmission for this trace is broken, and what was narrated by Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, in His Almighty’s statement, Qaf, is a name of the names of God Almighty, and what was proven from Mujahid is that it is a letter of the alphabet, like His Almighty’s statement: Sad, “Nun,” Ha Meem, “Ta Seen,” Alif Lam Meem, and the like, so this distances what was mentioned previously from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. And it was said: What is meant is that the matter was decided by God, and that His statement, may His praise be exalted, Qaf, he said: It indicated what was omitted from the rest of the word, like the poet’s statement: I told her to stop and she said stop This interpretation should be considered because deletion in speech only occurs if there is evidence for it. How can this be understood from the mention of this letter? And the Almighty’s statement: And the Glorious Qur’an meaning the noble and great one “which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it. It is sent down by One Full of Wisdom, Praiseworthy.” They differed over the answer to the oath: What is it? Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of some grammarians that the Almighty’s statement: We know what the earth takes of them, and with Us is a record that preserves. There is some doubt about this, rather the answer is the content of the speech after the oath, which is the proof of prophethood and the proof of the Resurrection and its confirmation and realization, even if the oath does not meet in wording. This is common in the oaths of the Qur’an, as mentioned previously in His statement: “Sad. By the Qur’an full of remembrance. But those who disbelieve are in arrogance and dissension.” And likewise He said here: “Qaf. By the glorious Qur’an. But they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves. So the disbelievers say, “This is an amazing thing.” That is, they wondered at the sending of a messenger to them from among human beings, like His statement, the Most High: Is it a wonder to people that We have inspired a man from among themselves, ‘Warn the people?’ That is, this is not amazing, for God chooses messengers from among the angels and from among the people. Then the Almighty said, informing about them and their amazement at the Resurrection and their rejection of its occurrence: If we die and become dust, is that a far-fetched return? That is, they say: If we die and decay and our joints are severed and we become dust, how is it possible to return after that to this structure and composition? “If we die and decay and become dust, how is it possible to return after that to this structure and composition?” That is a far-fetched return That is, it is far-fetched to occur. The meaning is that they believe it is impossible and improbable. God the Almighty said in response to them: We certainly know what the earth takes of them That is, what it consumes of their bodies as they decay. We know that, and it is not hidden from Us where the bodies were dispersed, where they went, and where they went. And with Us is a Book that preserves That is, it preserves. Therefore, knowledge is comprehensive, and the Book also contains all things recorded. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the words of God the Almighty: We know what the earth takes from them, meaning what it eats of their flesh, skin, bones and hair. This is what Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and others said. Then God the Almighty explained the reason for their disbelief, stubbornness and their rejection of what is not far-fetched, saying: Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused state, meaning this is the state of everyone who deviates from the truth. Whatever he says after that is false. Confusion is something that is different, disturbed, ambiguous and denied through its parts, like the words of God the Almighty: “Indeed, you are in a different statement. He who turns away from it is turned away from it.”

50:6: The Almighty says, alerting the servants to His great power, by which He revealed what is greater than what they were amazed at, considering it unlikely to happen: Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We have constructed it and adorned it meaning with lamps, and there are no rifts in it? They will not ask for anything but that it will rain on them. Katheer said: If God, the Most High, lets me witness that, I will say: We have been rained on by adorned slave girls. God the Almighty said: And with Us is more is like His saying: For those who have done good is the best and even more. It was mentioned previously in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Suhaib bin Sinan al-Rumi that it means looking at the Noble Face of God. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Sharik al-Qadi, on the authority of Uthman ibn Umair Abi al-Yaqzan, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And with Us is more, he said: The Lord Almighty appears to them every Friday. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is this? He said: This Friday has given you and your nation preference. People follow the Jews and Christians on it, and there is good for you in it. There is an hour for you in it when no believer supplicates to God Almighty for good, but it will be answered for him, and with Us it is the Day of More. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: O Gabriel, what is the Day of More? He (peace be upon him) said: “Indeed, your Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, has taken a valley in Paradise in which are filled with dunes of musk. When it is Friday, God sends down whomever He wills of His angels, and around it are pulpits of light upon which are the seats of the prophets. Those pulpits are surrounded by gold, crowned with rubies and emeralds, upon which are the martyrs and the truthful. They sit behind them on those dunes, and God, the Almighty, says: ‘I am your Lord, I have fulfilled My promise to you, so ask Me and I will give you.’ They say: ‘Our Lord, we ask You for Your pleasure.’ He says: ‘I am pleased with you, and upon Me you will have what you wish for, and I have more.’” They love Friday because of the goodness their Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, gives them on it. It is the day on which your Lord ascended to the Throne, on which He created Adam, and on which the Hour will come. This is how Imam Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, mentioned it in the book Al-Jumu’ah in Al-Umm, and it has chains of transmission on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir mentioned this hadith on the authority of Uthman bin Umair on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, in a more detailed manner than this, and he mentioned here a lengthy narration on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, that is attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it contains many strange things. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Darraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A man in Paradise will recline in Paradise for seventy years before he moves. Then a woman will come to him and strike him on the shoulder, and he will look at her face in her cheek, clearer than a mirror. The smallest pearl on her will illuminate what is between the east and the west. She will greet him and he will return the greeting and ask her, ‘Who are you?’ She will say, ‘I am from Al-Mazid.’ She will be wearing seventy garments, the smallest of which will be like a pearl of Tuba, and his sight will penetrate them until he can see the marrow of her shin behind it. She will be wearing crowns, the smallest pearl of which will illuminate what is between the east and the west.” This is how Abdullah bin Wahb narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith on the authority of Darraj.

He (peace be upon him) said: “Indeed, your Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, has taken a valley in Paradise in which are filled with dunes of musk. When it is Friday, God sends down whomever He wills of His angels, and around it are pulpits of light upon which are the seats of the prophets. Those pulpits are surrounded by gold, crowned with rubies and emeralds, upon which are the martyrs and the truthful. They sit behind them on those dunes, and God, the Almighty, says: ‘I am your Lord, I have fulfilled My promise to you, so ask Me and I will give you.’ They say: ‘Our Lord, we ask You for Your pleasure.’ He says: ‘I am pleased with you, and upon Me you will have what you wish for, and I have more.’” They love Friday because of the goodness their Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, gives them on it. It is the day on which your Lord ascended to the Throne, on which He created Adam, and on which the Hour will come. This is how Imam Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, mentioned it in the book Al-Jumu’ah in Al-Umm, and it has chains of transmission on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir mentioned this hadith on the authority of Uthman bin Umair on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, in a more detailed manner than this, and he mentioned here a lengthy narration on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, that is attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it contains many strange things. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Darraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A man in Paradise will recline in Paradise for seventy years before he moves. Then a woman will come to him and strike him on the shoulder, and he will look at her face in her cheek, clearer than a mirror. The smallest pearl on her will illuminate what is between the east and the west. She will greet him and he will return the greeting and ask her, ‘Who are you?’ She will say, ‘I am from Al-Mazid.’ She will be wearing seventy garments, the smallest of which will be like a pearl of Tuba, and his sight will penetrate them until he can see the marrow of her shin behind it. She will be wearing crowns, the smallest pearl of which will illuminate what is between the east and the west.” This is how Abdullah bin Wahb narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith on the authority of Darraj.

50:40: God the Almighty says: And how many a generation before these deniers have We destroyed who were mightier than them in strike meaning they were more numerous and stronger than them and they tilled the earth and populated it more than they tilled it. That is why God the Almighty said here: “And they searched through the lands. Is there any escape?” Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: They tilled it. Mujahid said: And they searched through the lands means they traveled through the land. Qatada said: They traveled through the lands, meaning they traveled through them seeking provisions, trade, and earnings more than you have traveled through them. And it is said of one who travels through the lands that he has dug through them. Imru’ al-Qais said: I searched the horizons until I was satisfied with the spoils of return God the Almighty said: Is there any escape? That is, was there any escape for them from God’s decree and predestination? Did what they gathered benefit them, and was God’s punishment averted from them when it came to them when they denied the messengers? So you too have no escape, no way out, no way out, and no way out. God the Almighty said: Indeed in that is a reminder That is, a lesson for whoever has a heart That is, a mind with which he comprehends. Mujahid said: a mind or listens while he is present That is, listens to the speech, comprehends it, and understands it with his mind. Mujahid said: or listens That is, he does not think about this with his heart. Ad-Dahhak said: The Arabs say someone listened with his ears, and he is present with his heart and not absent. This is what Ath-Thawri and others said. And the saying of the Almighty: And We certainly created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us is a confirmation of the Resurrection, because He who was able to create the heavens and the earth and did not tire in creating them is able to revive the dead by a fortiori and more appropriate way. Qatada said: The Jews - may God’s curses be upon them - said that God created the heavens and the earth in six days, then He rested on the seventh day, which is the Sabbath, and they call it the Day of Rest. So God Almighty revealed the refutation of what they said and interpreted, And no weariness touched Us meaning no fatigue, exhaustion, or toil, as the Almighty said in another verse: Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth and did not tire in their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, He is over all things competent. And as the Almighty said: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. And the Almighty said: Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven which He constructed? And the Almighty said: So be patient over what they say meaning the deniers. Be patient with them and leave them with gracious leave. And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting. The obligatory prayers before the Isra’ were two, before the rising of the sun at the time of Fajr and before the setting at the time of Asr. The night prayer was obligatory upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and upon his nation for a year, then its obligation was abrogated for the nation. Then after that, God Almighty abrogated all of that on the Night of Isra’ with five prayers, but among them were the Fajr and Asr prayers, so they were before the rising of the sun and before the setting. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ narrated to us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid narrated to us, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of Jarir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: “You will be presented before your Lord and you will see Him as you see this moon, and you will not be wronged therein. So if you can avoid being overcome in prayer before sunrise and before sunset, then do so.” Then he recited: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and the rest of the group narrated it on the authority of Ismail. God the Almighty said: {And during part of the night, glorify Him} meaning, separate it from Him, as He said: {And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional act for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise}. {And after prostration} Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both: It is glorifying God after the prayer. This is supported by what was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him that he said: The poor emigrants came and said: O Messenger of God, the wealthy have acquired the highest ranks and eternal bliss. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And what is that? They said: They pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, they give in charity but we do not give in charity, they free slaves but we do not free slaves. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Shall I not teach you something which, if you do it, you will outpace those who come after you and no one will be better than you except he who does as you do? You glorify God, praise Him, and magnify God after every prayer thirty-three times.” They said: O Messenger of God, our wealthy brothers heard what we did and did the same. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is the grace of God which He bestows upon whom He wills. The second opinion is that what is meant by God Almighty’s saying: and the ends of prostration are the two rak’ahs after sunset. This was narrated on the authority of Umar, Ali and his son al-Hasan, Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, and Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with them. This is also what Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Sha’bi, al-Nakha’i, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others say. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ and Abdur-Rahman narrated to us from Sufyan from Abu Ishaq, from Asim ibn Damrah, from Ali may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to pray two rak’ahs after every prescribed prayer except Fajr and Asr. Abdur-Rahman said: After every prayer. Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan Ath-Thawri with this chain of transmission. An-Nasa’i and Mutraf added this chain of transmission from Abu Ishaq. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun ibn Ishaq Al-Hamadani narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Rushdin ibn Kurayb, from his father, from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, who said: I spent one night with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he prayed two short rak’ahs before Fajr. Then he went out to pray and said: O Ibn Abbas, Two rak’ahs before Fajr prayer after the stars have set, and two rak’ahs after Maghrib prayer after prostration. At-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abu Hisham Ar-Rifa’i, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl with this chain of transmission. He said: It is strange; we do not know it except from this source. The hadith of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him that he spent the night in the house of his aunt Maymunah may God be pleased with her and prayed thirteen rak'ahs with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that night is authentic in the two Sahihs and other collections. As for this addition, it is strange and is only known from this source. Rashdin ibn Kurayb is weak, and perhaps it is from the words of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and attributed to him. And God knows best.
50:41: God Almighty says: And listen O Muhammad to the Day when the crier will call from a place nearby Qatada said: Ka'b al-Ahbar said that God Almighty commands an angel to call out on the rock of the Holy House: "O decayed bones and dismembered limbs, God Almighty commands you to gather for the passing of judgment. "The Day they hear the Shout in truth" meaning the blowing of the Trumpet that will bring the truth about which most of them had doubts. "That is the Day of Resurrection" meaning from the graves. "Indeed, it is We who bring to life and cause to die, and to Us is the final destination" meaning He is the One who begins creation and then restores it, which is easier for Him, and to Him is the final destination of all creation. He will reward each one for his deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil. And the Almighty said: On the Day the earth will split open and reveal them swiftly. That is because God, the Almighty, will send down rain from the sky, with which the bodies of all creation will grow in their graves, just as water causes seeds to grow in the soil. When the bodies are complete, God, the Almighty, will command Israfil to blow the Trumpet. The souls have been deposited in a hole in the Trumpet. When Israfil blows it, the souls will emerge glowing between the sky and the earth. Then God, the Almighty, will say: By My glory and majesty, every soul will return to the body it inhabited. So every soul will return to its body and will move within it as poison moves within a stung person. The earth will split open and reveal them, and they will rise to the place of reckoning, rushing to the command of God, the Almighty, “Rushing to the Caller. The disbelievers will say, ‘This is a difficult day.’” And God, the Almighty, said: The Day He will call you, and you will respond with His praise and you will think that you had remained only a little. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the first from whom the earth will split open. And the Almighty’s saying: That is an easy gathering for Us means This is an easy repetition for us, easy for us as the Almighty said: And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye. God the Almighty said: “He did not create you and resurrect you except as one soul. Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing.” And His statement, We know best what they say, means that Our knowledge encompasses what the polytheists say to you of denial, so do not be alarmed by it, as in His statement: “And We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say. So exalt [God] with praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate. And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty.” And His statement, And you are not a compeller over them, means that you are not the one who compels these people to follow the right path, and that is not something you are charged with. Mujahid, Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: And you are not a tyrant over them, meaning do not be a tyrant over them. The first statement is better. If he had intended what they said, he would have said: And do not be a tyrant over them. Rather, he said: And you are not a tyrant over them, meaning you are not forcing them to believe; you are only a conveyor. Al-Farra’ said: I heard the Arabs say, So-and-so compelled so-and-so to do such-and-such, meaning he compelled him. Then God, the Almighty, said: So remind with the Qur’an whoever fears My threat, meaning, you should convey the message of your Lord, for only he who fears God and His threat and hopes for His promise will remember, like His statement: You are only responsible for conveying the message, and upon Us is the account. And His statement, the Almighty, the Majestic, “So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them.” You do not have to guide them, but God guides whom He wills. “Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills.” That is why God, the Almighty, said here: “And you are not a tyrant over them. So remind with the Qur’an whoever fears My threat.” Qatada used to say: O God, make us among those who fear Your threat and hope for Your promise, O Most Generous, Most Merciful. The last interpretation of Surat Qaf. Praise be to God alone, and God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.

The earth will split open and reveal them, and they will rise to the place of reckoning, rushing to the command of God, the Almighty, “Rushing to the Caller. The disbelievers will say, ‘This is a difficult day.’” And God, the Almighty, said: The Day He will call you, and you will respond with His praise and you will think that you had remained only a little. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the first from whom the earth will split open. And the Almighty’s saying: That is an easy gathering for Us means This is an easy repetition for us, easy for us as the Almighty said: And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye. God the Almighty said: “He did not create you and resurrect you except as one soul. Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing.” And His statement, We know best what they say, means that Our knowledge encompasses what the polytheists say to you of denial, so do not be alarmed by it, as in His statement: “And We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say. So exalt [God] with praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate. And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty.” And His statement, And you are not a compeller over them, means that you are not the one who compels these people to follow the right path, and that is not something you are charged with. Mujahid, Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: And you are not a tyrant over them, meaning do not be a tyrant over them. The first statement is better. If he had intended what they said, he would have said: And do not be a tyrant over them. Rather, he said: And you are not a tyrant over them, meaning you are not forcing them to believe; you are only a conveyor. Al-Farra’ said: I heard the Arabs say, So-and-so compelled so-and-so to do such-and-such, meaning he compelled him. Then God, the Almighty, said: So remind with the Qur’an whoever fears My threat, meaning, you should convey the message of your Lord, for only he who fears God and His threat and hopes for His promise will remember, like His statement: You are only responsible for conveying the message, and upon Us is the account. And His statement, the Almighty, the Majestic, “So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them.” You do not have to guide them, but God guides whom He wills. “Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills.” That is why God, the Almighty, said here: “And you are not a tyrant over them. So remind with the Qur’an whoever fears My threat.” Qatada used to say: O God, make us among those who fear Your threat and hope for Your promise, O Most Generous, Most Merciful. The last interpretation of Surat Qaf. Praise be to God alone, and God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.
